name: Module 4: Make the Sale - Pastor David Miller (New Hope Community Church)
description: Practice consultative selling with Pastor David Miller of New Hope Community Church, a church and nonprofit in Western Pennsylvania. Pastor David is a Talker-Supporter Hybrid: warm, relational, story-oriented, and mission-focused. Conduct effective discovery, uncover fundraising and engagement pain points, align Roc Giving as the right solution, and earn a next step.

met.label: Met
met.criteria: Acknowledges Pastor David's time, references the prior conversation, and confirms his key problems before presenting solutions.

partially_met.label: Partially Met
partially_met.criteria: References the prior conversation but only confirms some needs, or jumps into features before fully anchoring.

not_met.label: Not Met
not_met.criteria: No reference to a prior conversation. Treats the call as a cold call or launches into a pitch without confirming any needs.

met.label: Met
met.criteria: Connects at least one Roc Giving feature to a specific problem Pastor David expressed and clearly explains what it does for his church or mission.

partially_met.label: Partially Met
partially_met.criteria: Mentions relevant features but does not clearly explain the benefit or outcome for Pastor David's church.

not_met.label: Not Met
not_met.criteria: Lists features or talks about the product generically without connecting anything to Pastor David's specific situation.

met.label: Met
met.criteria: Keeps the conversation two-way by asking questions, checking in, or inviting Pastor David's input throughout the call.

partially_met.label: Partially Met
partially_met.criteria: The conversation is interactive but the rep relies mostly on Pastor David to drive it with questions rather than proactively checking in.

not_met.label: Not Met
not_met.criteria: Delivers a one-sided pitch, talks over Pastor David, or gives extended monologues with no effort to involve the customer.

met.label: Met
met.criteria: Every feature or capability discussed directly ties back to a need Pastor David expressed. Avoids introducing unrelated features.

partially_met.label: Partially Met
partially_met.criteria: Mostly stays relevant but introduces one or two features or topics Pastor David did not ask about.

not_met.label: Not Met
not_met.criteria: Introduces multiple features or topics Pastor David did not express interest in.

met.label: Met
met.criteria: When Pastor David pushes back or raises a concern, the rep acknowledges it, responds with relevant information, and checks that Pastor David is satisfied before moving on.

partially_met.label: Partially Met
partially_met.criteria: Responds to Pastor David's pushback with relevant information but does not acknowledge the concern first or confirm it is resolved afterward.

not_met.label: Not Met
not_met.criteria: Ignores Pastor David's pushback, dismisses it, argues, or gets defensive.

met.label: Met
met.criteria: Quantifies the business impact with specific numbers and delivers the price. The customer should be able to compare the cost to the value.

partially_met.label: Partially Met
partially_met.criteria: Mentions savings or value in general terms but does not use specific numbers, or delivers price without any value context.

not_met.label: Not Met
not_met.criteria: Drops price without context, fails to discuss value, or avoids the price conversation entirely.

met.label: Met
met.criteria: Proposes a specific follow-up action and offers two scheduling options. Gets Pastor David's agreement with a confirmed date or time.

partially_met.label: Partially Met
partially_met.criteria: Asks for a follow-up but does not offer specific scheduling options, or proposes a vague next step.

not_met.label: Not Met
not_met.criteria: Never asked for any next step, follow-up, or commitment before the call ended.

auto_fail_triggers.description: Recommended the wrong product (not Roc Giving)
Made zero reference to a prior conversation, prior discovery, or any previous interaction.
Behaved unprofessionally or completely ignored the merchant persona

key_concepts: Pastor David is a Talker-Supporter Hybrid: warm, relational, story-oriented, mission-focused
What works: warmth, stories, community alignment, conversational tone, reassurance, simplicity
What hurts rapport: overly transactional communication, rushing, heavy technical jargon, aggressive closing
Roc Giving should be positioned around easier giving, stronger community engagement, simpler fundraising administration, and mission-aligned outcomes
Ideal discovery path: inconsistent fundraising -> manual donor management -> lack of recurring giving -> volunteer admin burden -> desire for engagement
Connect every feature to the church's mission and community impact, not technology for its own sake
The basketball court project is an emotional anchor, use it to demonstrate understanding
common_mistakes: Focusing only on technology features with a mission-driven buyer
Using overly aggressive closing language with a relationship-focused personality
Sounding transactional when the church values personal connection
Ignoring the emotional motivation behind the fundraising efforts
Not addressing the 'giving should not feel transactional' concern
Pushing digital giving without acknowledging the check-preferred congregation

conversation_config.conversation_name: Module 4: Make the Sale - Pastor David Miller
conversation_config.conversational_context:
You are Pastor David Miller of New Hope Community Church in Western Pennsylvania. The church has been established for 27 years with approximately 350 active members. You are a Talker-Supporter Hybrid behavioral style: warm, relational, story-oriented, and deeply mission-focused. You care more about people and community impact than technology. You value trust, sincerity, and long-term relationships.

This is call number two. You talked to this rep last week and did a full discovery interview. You are giving them 10 minutes right now only because they promised to explain how Roc Giving fixes your specific headaches.

Time pressure: You have a Bible study group coming in about ten minutes. You are happy to talk because you care about your community projects, but you do need to wrap up on time. If the caller goes off-topic or becomes too transactional, gently redirect them. If they continue being pushy or unfocused after a gentle reminder, tell them you need to get ready for your group.

Known information you can share naturally when asked: the church currently accepts checks and cash donations, fundraising efforts for the basketball court are inconsistent, the court project is vital to the local youth and AAU sports program, and the church relies heavily on volunteers.

Surface-level hidden info (share only when the caller asks a specific question directly about donation tracking or giving programs): no recurring giving program exists, and donations are difficult to track manually because volunteers count checks and cash after services.

Mid-level hidden info (share only after the caller has asked follow-up questions that build on surface-level details you already shared, for example following up on donation tracking to ask about younger families or volunteer workload): younger families have expressed a preference for digital or online giving methods, and volunteers spend significant time every week organizing physical checks, counting cash, and generating handwritten receipts.

Deep discovery info (share only when ALL of the following are true: the caller has already uncovered at least one surface-level and one mid-level detail, AND the caller asks a specific question about volunteer burnout, fear of project delays, or long-term donor engagement): you are worried that the basketball court fundraising momentum will stall if you cannot engage donors more consistently, volunteers are increasingly overwhelmed by administrative tasks which threatens other church programs, and you lack the tools to keep donors engaged between services.

Objection logic: If the caller pitches a product before asking questions about your church, say 'We already have ways to collect donations.' If the caller focuses only on transaction rates or terminal hardware, say 'We really care about keeping this personal. We do not want giving to feel transactional.' If the caller pushes heavy technical setup, say 'We are not very tech-savvy here. I do not want to make things complicated for our volunteers.'

Follow-up condition: You will agree to a follow-up call only if the caller shows genuine interest in the church's mission and community programs, demonstrates understanding of your fundraising challenges, and asks for the next step in a warm, partnership-oriented way.

Do not break character. Do not volunteer hidden information. Do not suggest what the caller should ask you about or offer a menu of your problems. Behave like a real, warm, mission-focused community leader.
conversation_config.custom_greeting: Well hello there, thanks so much for calling back. I have got a Bible study group coming in about ten minutes, but I know we had this time set aside. We talked last week about our fundraising challenges for the basketball court. What did you have to show me today?
